theorem_read.label: Theorem 2.1 (the one leg 313 carried at summary level)
theorem_read.hypothesis_verbatim: Let V(y,s) in C^2_x C^1_t (R^{3+1}) be a time periodic solution of (1.6) with period S_0 > 0 that has bounded first derivatives and satisfies (2.1) lim_{|y|->infty} V(y,s) = 0, for all s in [0,S_0), and for some r > 0, (2.2) Omega := curl V in intersection_{0<q<r} L^q(R^3 x [0,S_0]). Then V = 0 on R^{3+1}.
theorem_read.equation_1_6_verbatim: d_s V + (alpha/(alpha+1)) V + (1/(alpha+1)) (y . grad) V + (V . grad) V = -grad P, div V = 0
theorem_read.equation_1_6_is: the self-similar transform of (E), the EULER equations; there is no Laplacian term
theorem_read.equation_1_10_verbatim: dV/ds - Laplacian V - a V - a y.grad V + (V.grad)V = -grad P, div V = 0
theorem_read.equation_1_10_is: the Navier-Stokes rescaled (time-dependent Leray) equation, displayed separately in subsection 1.1 'Related results for Navier-Stokes equations'; NO theorem in the paper is stated for it
theorem_read.authors_own_reach_remark_verbatim: Remark after the proof: The above proof works for more general system (2.9) V_s + a V + b (y . grad) V + (V . grad) V = -grad P, div V = 0, where a, b are arbitrary real constants with b != 0.
theorem_read.reach_remark_note: The generalisation is over the two CONSTANTS a and b. -Laplacian V is not a member of that family for any choice of a, b. This is the load-bearing clause: the authors state exactly how far their proof carries, and it carries to a two-parameter family of INVISCID rescaled equations.

paper_own_status_report.backward_dss_ns_verbatim: The existence of backward DSS solutions has not been addressed in literature, except that if V in L^inf(R, L^3(R^3)), which is equivalent to v in L^inf((-infty,0), L^3(R^3)), it must be zero by the result of [12]. Thus one is concerned, e.g., if V only has the bound (1.11) |V(y,s)| <= C_*/(1+|y|), for all (y,s) in R^{3+1}, for some large constant C_*.
paper_own_status_report.lambda_remark_verbatim: In view of the forward case, one may hope that the case with the DSS-factor lambda sufficiently close to 1 might be easier to exclude.
paper_own_status_report.implication_1: The paper itself declares the backward-DSS-NS question OPEN, in 2013, in its own words.
paper_own_status_report.implication_2: The only backward-DSS-NS exclusion it credits is V in L^inf(R,L^3) (Sverak [12]) -- and the screened object's clause (delta) specifies the profile OUTSIDE L^inf_t L^3. The two definitions do not overlap.
paper_own_status_report.implication_3: The screened object's clause (gamma), lambda significantly larger than 1, is on the side the authors flag as the HARDER one -- and that is within Euler, before viscosity is reached.

alpha_equation.reason: Every theorem hypothesises 'a time periodic solution of (1.6)', and (1.6) is the rescaled EULER system. The screened object solves Navier-Stokes. The authors' own reach remark extends the proof to arbitrary real constants a, b with b != 0, and NOT to the addition of -Laplacian V.

decay_hypothesis.reason: (2.2) requires Omega in L^q(R^3 x [0,S_0]) for EVERY q in (0,r). Small q makes L^q integrability at infinity a severe decay demand (|Omega| must decay faster than |y|^{-3/q}, which blows up as q -> 0). The screened object carries only a Type-I-scale bound of the shape (1.11), |V| <= C_*/(1+|y|), which the paper introduces as the case NOT covered. This CONFIRMS the 'merely a decaying subclass' horn leg 313 named and refused to guess.

gamma_lambda.reason: Screened object: lambda significantly larger than 1. Paper: lambda sufficiently close to 1 'might be easier to exclude'.

beta_symmetry.reason: The hypothesis fails before symmetry becomes relevant. Recorded only to close the ledger of four clauses.

gate.why_not_the_ambiguous_branch: The paper names its equation in its title, its abstract, every theorem statement, and its own remark on how far the proof generalises. Nothing is ambiguous. The unknown leg 313 recorded honestly is now KNOWN.
